title: Ivo and the Autopsy
premise: Orsen Iversen, a true-crime podcaster who has spent a decade narrating other people's tragedies, is pulled into one of their own when a corpse wearing clothes from Orsen's closet surfaces in the flooded quarry outside the town of Vesterhavn. The body belongs to a man who vanished thirty years ago on the night of the Halvorsen family's anniversary dinner, and the autopsy reveals details only someone intimate with the case could know. As Orsen excavates alibis that were woven and rehearsed decades ago, they realize their own family's silence was never innocence but complicity, and that someone inside the investigation is feeding them truth and lies in equal measure. At the anniversary dinner, where the surviving Halvorsens gather to toast thirty untroubled years, Orsen finally names the killer, forcing a confession that shatters the town's founding myth, though it costs them the last person they trusted.
about_author: Astrid Delacroix is the pen name of a former forensic archivist who spent eleven years cataloguing unsolved cases before turning to fiction. She writes mysteries obsessed with the paperwork of death: the reports, the silences, and the small lies people file away like evidence.

chapters.title: The Clothes Make the Corpse
chapters.summary: Orsen Iversen, POV. A body pulled from the flooded quarry wears Orsen's own missing jacket and scarf, items stolen from their car weeks earlier. The police treat Orsen as a suspect; the podcast audience treats them as bait. Emotional beat: the voyeur becomes the viewed, and invisibility dies in a single morning.

chapters.title: Thirty Years of Quiet
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. The victim is identified as Mikkel Brandt, who vanished in 1994 on the night of the Halvorsen anniversary dinner, the coldest case on record and the subject of Orsen's stalled podcast season. Detective Sana Reyes grudgingly shares the file. Beat: old dread resurfaces as Orsen realizes they grew up three streets from this mystery.

chapters.title: What the Water Kept
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV, intercut with the pathologist's report. The autopsy shows injuries consistent with the original 1994 theory, but also a detail never made public: a broken signet ring lodged under a rib. Only investigators and the family knew about the ring. Beat: the case isn't cold; it's curated.

chapters.title: The Anniversary Guest List
chapters.summary: Orsen interviews the surviving Halvorsens: patriarch Einar, his daughter Liv, and son Anders, all polished and rehearsed after three decades of retelling. Their alibis are seamless, too seamless. Beat: loyalty performed so well it looks like choreography.

chapters.title: A Voice from the Archive
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Digging through 1994 case tapes for the podcast, Orsen finds an interview with a witness whose testimony was quietly dropped: a housekeeper named Grethe who saw a second car that night. She died in 2001. Beat: the thrill of discovery shadowed by the suspicion that someone wanted this tape found.

chapters.title: Reyes's Ledger
chapters.summary: Detective Sana Reyes, POV. Reyes reveals she inherited the case from her mentor, Inspector Dahl, whose notes contain a page torn out. She warns Orsen off but slips them Dahl's address book. Beat: two investigators circling trust neither can afford.

chapters.title: The House That Forgot
chapters.summary: Orsen visits Dahl, now retired and failing, at a care home outside Vesterhavn. Dahl mistakes Orsen for someone else, murmuring 'you wore his coat' before going silent. Beat: horror blooming gently, the sense of being recognized by a stranger.

chapters.title: Alibi, Rehearsed
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Cross-referencing the 1994 statements, Orsen notices the Halvorsens' accounts use identical phrasing, word for word, across separate interviews. They were coached, or worse, written. Beat: the vertigo of realizing a whole town learned its lines.

chapters.title: Someone Is Listening
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. A leaked clip of Orsen's unpublished episode airs on local radio, twisting their words into an accusation against Liv Halvorsen. Orsen's producer quits, fearing liability. Beat: isolation deepening; the podcast that gave Orsen power now turns it against them.

chapters.title: Anders Breaks Ranks
chapters.summary: Anders Halvorsen, POV. Drunk and frightened, Anders approaches Orsen to say he never believed his father's story about that night, but if he talks, he loses everything: the business, the name, the inheritance. Beat: loyalty versus truth made flesh in one compromised man.

chapters.title: The Second Car
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Tracing the registration from Grethe's testimony, Orsen finds the second car belonged to the town's former coroner, Dr. Halloran, who signed the original (empty) autopsy and left Vesterhavn soon after. Beat: the machinery of cover-up clicking into view.

chapters.title: Dinner Invitations
chapters.summary: Orsen receives a formal invitation to the Halvorsens' thirtieth anniversary dinner, unsigned except by Einar himself. Reyes warns it's a trap; Orsen decides being inside the room beats being outside it. Beat: dread braided with ambition.

chapters.title: Halloran's Confession, Half of It
chapters.summary: Orsen tracks Halloran to a coastal town. Dying of emphysema, he admits he falsified the 1994 finding of accidental drowning but claims he was paid by someone he'll only name face to face, at the dinner. He dies before saying more. Beat: hope snatched away, stakes raised.

chapters.title: The Torn Page
chapters.summary: Reyes, POV. Reyes reconstructs Dahl's missing page from microfilm: it named a suspect in 1994 and was removed the day before Dahl's forced early retirement. The handwriting matches Einar Halvorsen's correspondence with the mayor. Beat: corruption revealed as institutional, not personal.

chapters.title: Whose Coat Was It
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Forensics confirms the clothes on the body were altered to fit the corpse, tailored, not merely worn. Whoever dressed the body knew Orsen's measurements. The implication lands: this murder was staged for Orsen specifically. Beat: paranoia cresting; the story was always about them.

chapters.title: Liv's Version
chapters.summary: Liv Halvorsen, POV. Liv privately tells Orsen that Mikkel Brandt came to the dinner that night to confront Einar over money laundering that built the family fortune, and that she saw her father follow him out. She never told because Einar saved her from ruin once, long ago. Beat: sympathy complicating suspicion.

chapters.title: The Producer's Return
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Orsen's estranged brother Tomas, who produced the podcast's first season, reappears offering help, but Orsen finds Tomas's fingerprints on the leaked radio clip and a receipt for dry cleaning dated the week Orsen's clothes went missing. Beat: betrayal arriving from the safest direction.

chapters.title: Anniversary
chapters.summary: Orsen attends the dinner. Toasts are raised; Einar performs magnificence. Orsen lays out the ring, the ledger, Halloran's half-confession before the assembled guests, and watches which face breaks first. It is not Einar's. Beat: the climax ignites, truth as a weapon drawn at the table.

chapters.title: The One Who Wove It
chapters.summary: Climax continues, Orsen's POV. Tomas confesses: he killed Mikkel in 1994 as a young man protecting Einar, his real father, then spent thirty years curating the silence, including staging the body in Orsen's clothes to control the narrative when Reyes reopened the file. He kept Orsen close the whole time. Beat: the devastating fusion of loyalty, corruption, and identity.

chapters.title: Glass on the Floor
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. In the chaos after the confession, Einar tries to buy the room's silence one final time; Liv, choosing truth over blood, hands Reyes the ledger pages she has hidden for decades. Tomas is arrested on the terrace where Mikkel died. Beat: power collapsing under its own weight.

chapters.title: Final Episode
chapters.summary: Orsen records the last episode of the season, telling the whole story including their own blindness and Tomas's betrayal, and releases it unedited. The town reacts with grief and relief in equal measure; Reyes closes the case formally. Beat: mourning and catharsis entwined.

chapters.title: After the Autopsy
chapters.summary: Orsen, epilogue POV. Months later, Orsen visits Mikkel Brandt's grave, finally marked with his name, and leaves the repaired signet ring. Invisible no longer, they begin a new series about the people history overlooked. Beat: quiet resolution; identity rebuilt from truth rather than silence.
